Class AnimatedAreaAnalysisCase

java.lang.Object
sysmlinjava.common.SysMLAnything
sysmlinjava.occurrences.SysMLOccurrence
sysmlinjava.actions.SysMLAction
sysmlinjava.actions.SysMLCalculation
sysmlinjava.actions.SysMLCase
sysmlinjava.analysis.SysMLAnalysisCase
sysmlinjava.analysis.ParametricAnalysisCase
sysmlinjava.views.animatedareadisplay.AnimatedAreaAnalysisCase
All Implemented Interfaces:
AttributeObserver, ObservableAttribute, StateBehaviorContext
public abstract class AnimatedAreaAnalysisCase extends ParametricAnalysisCase
AnimatedAreaAnalysisCase is an executable model of a SysML analysis case that produces an animated display of objects whose states and positions are represented by the current values of the analysis parameters.

AnimatedAreaAnalysisCase extends the basic ParametericAnalysisCase. As such, the analysis case defines a set of parameters which are "bound" to the part attributes that correspond to the parameters. The analysis calculation calculates the area display from these analysis parameters.

As an abstract class, the AnimatedAreaAnalysisCase must be extended/specialized for the particular area display that is to be generated. Specializations may use the parameters defined in this base class, i.e. the Point2D-type and Points2D-type parameters for the most commonly used parameters for an area display, i.e. object positions, but may also define other anslysis parameters in the specialized class as needed to further specialize the area display. In any case, the specalized AnimatedAreaAnalysisCase must override and invoke the AnalysisCaseAction operation to calculate the displayData for the animated display.

As described in the ParametricAnalysisCase comments, the analysis parameters must be connected (bound) to the part attributes that correspond to the analysis parameters via the SysMLBindingConnector. These binding connectors must be created in the createBindingConnectors() method in a part that contains the AnimatedAreaAnalysisCase specialization as well as the specialized SysMLPart that contains the bound attriutes.

    • AnimatedAreaAnalysisCase

      public AnimatedAreaAnalysisCase(int udpPort, boolean logToConsole)
      Constructor
      Parameters:
      udpPort - number of UDP port on which to receive the display definition and data
      logToConsole - whether to send all transmit() logs to console. Note: transmit() operation can log every object's toString() string to the console. The more frequently log messages are sent to console, the greater the CPU resources are needed. This can cause noticable slowing of the console display and related applications.

    • perform

      public void perform()
      Overridable method to perform the analysis on the current values of the set of analysis parameters. The method should be overidden to perform the actual analysis and/or invoke this perform() method to perform the action function declared to perform the analysis. In any case, the override method should lastly invoke the transmitChartData() operation to calculate and transmit the animated area display data for display.

    • createResultEvaluation

      protected void createResultEvaluation()
      Description copied from class: SysMLAnalysisCase
      Overridable operation that creates the result evaluation of the analysis case, i.e. the action to be performed to evaluate the result. An example follows: 
      			public class MyAnalysisCase extends SysMLAnalysisCase
			{
					:
				&#64;AnalysisResultEvalution
				FirstResultEvaluation firstEval;
				&#64;AnalysisResultEvalution
				LastResultEvaluation lastEval;
					:
				protected void createResultEvaluation()
				{
					firstEval = new FirstResultEvaluation(this);
					lastEval = new LastResultEvaluation(this);
				}
			}
      Note the example uses two result evaluations, both of which are presuemd to be specializations of the SysMLAction. However, evaluation could be performed by methods declared in the SysMLAnalysisCase and annotated as @AnalysisResultEvaluations, in lieue of annotated method(s) in lieu of creating a SysMLAction as shown here.
      Overrides:
      createResultEvaluation in class SysMLAnalysisCase

    • stop

      public void stop()
      Description copied from class: ParametricAnalysisCase
      Stops the part's state machine-based behavior, if a state machine is present in the part. The operation simply stops the state machine execution. Note if this part's state machine is asynchronous, i.e. executes in its own thread, then this operation imposes a "hard stop" where the thread is canceled regardless of what state it's in. If the part's state machine is synchronous, this operation can only queue up a FinalEvent to the event queue, on the assumption that the state machine is capable of handling the FinalEvent at the point in which the stop() method is invoked. Therefore, if a part is synchronous and this stop method is used, it's state machine should be modeled to handle the FinalEvent accordingly.
      Specified by:
